newsitem.title: CANADA: NOVA compressor outage to start Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: NOVA compressor outage to start Wednesday.

text.p: A scheduled compressor station outage on NOVA Corp's NOVA Gas Transmission system in Alberta was expected to take 1.2 billion cubic feet of gas per day off the pipeline network, a NOVA spokesman said on Wednesday.
Traders said the outage was lifting prices for spot natural gas in Alberta.

The outage at the Knight compressor station, about 180 km northwest of Edmonton, was scheduled to last for 36 hours starting at 1600 MDT (1800 EDT/2200 GMT) on Wednesday, said NOVA's Paul Clark. The station is on the Edson mainline, which runs from Zama in the northwest corner of Alberta.
"We're doing a little equipment installation at Knight," he said.
A second 36-hour phase, slated to start at 0600 MDT (0800 EDT/1200 GMT) on September 23, will restrict about 950 million cubic feet per day to conduct in-line inspection of the Knight work, he said.
"This is a scheduled outage, so nobody is hysterical about it. All of our customers were informed several months ago," Clark said.
The outage, coupled with about 800 million cubic feet per day of gas being injected into Alberta storage facilities, saw spot gas prices surge in the province, traders said.
Day-to-day prices at the AECO storage hub were quoted at about C$1.26 per gigajoule, up from about C$1.15 on Tuesday.
Also providing strength was the end earlier this week of maintenance work at AECO, said a Calgary-based marketer.
"Prices have trended up all week," he said, adding that he traded gas last weekend for well below C$1. "Most of it has to do with the outage, though."
